## Try: a skill {#try-skills .your-turn background-color="#f1c84b"}

In `pivot-interviews`, after the quote check:

::: {.prompt}
Turn the quote check we just did into a skill called check-quotes.
:::

Then: *"What skills do you have?"* And next time, in another folder: *"Check the
quotes in this report."*

[You never touch the file format. Most things work fine without skills.]{.small}

## Try: subagents {#try-subagents .your-turn background-color="#f1c84b"}

In `pivot-interviews`:

::: {.prompt}
Use subagents, one per transcript. Each returns three lines: what triggered the
change, who pushed for it, and one quote. Then put them in one table.
:::

[Both tools can do this. Watch the helpers start and finish.]{.small}

## Any other word? {#other}

**Ask the tool.** Two sentences, for a professor:

::: {.prompt}
What is [a word you've heard]? Two sentences, for a professor. Then: would it
help with my research?
:::

[The same move as Thursday: unsure what something is? Ask.]{.punch}
